# Preface.

What a great scandal is given to the enemies of the Evangelical Truth <note>The "Evangelical Truth" refers to the Protestant, specifically Lutheran, faith.</note> when open strife arises among brothers of the same religious fellowship and is made public through the press; every impartial heart can easily see this. Yet it is as clear as day and cannot be denied—indeed, one would have to be a stranger in Israel <note>A biblical idiom (from Luke 24:18) meaning someone who is completely ignorant of well-known local events.</note> not to know the disputes into which the leaders of our churches fell among themselves after the death of Luther. ### §. 1.

It might not be unfairly asked by an inquisitive person whether everything Saint John saw here in Heaven was nothing but a mere representation of the ancient **Tabernacle** <term>original: *Stifts-Hutten*; the portable dwelling-place of God used by the Israelites during the Exodus</term> of the **Mosaic service**; or whether that Mosaic one was instead a representation of this heavenly one? However, as inquisitive as this may seem, it is equally useful for a contemplative person, who, after diligent reflection on both, will above all else hold the following propositions to be true. Namely, firstly **1.** The **Divine Being** is infinite according to His presence; whereas even the most noble and highest **creature** <note>In this context, "creature" (German: *Creatur*) refers to any created being, including humans and angels, as opposed to the uncreated Creator.</note> among all has only a finite and circumscribed spatiality. Therefore David says that His greatness has no end, Psalm 145:3. And **Zophar** of Naama <note>referring to Zophar the Naamathite, one of the three friends of Job</note>; "Can you find Him out by searching? He is higher than Heaven; what will you do? He is deeper than Hell; and how will you know (Him)? His measure is longer than the Earth, and broader than the sea," Job 11:8. And **Baruch**: "He is great and has no end, the Most High and immeasurable," Chapter 3:25. Therefore, creatures are to be counted against Him like a drop in a water bucket; and like a speck of dust on the scales! Yes, even as nothing, Isaiah 40:15, 17. Daniel 4:32. Indeed, the whole world is before Him like the pointer on the scales, and like a drop of morning dew. Wisdom of Solomon 11:23.

### §. 2. 

Furthermore, that the **Divine Being** is **incorporeal**, **invisible**; also **incomprehensible** in Himself; and that something finite cannot grasp anything infinite.

who could oversee the infinite God all at once? Nor could it happen through mere intellectual contemplation / as which can never occur without an **Idea** <note>original: *Idea*; here meaning a mental image or conceptual model</note> or a fashioned representation / even in the Highest Spirits : nor through the union of one Essence with the other : For then it is indeed impossible to fill the entire Immeasurability into a small measure; nor in any other way / unless it be by means of a certain **Economy** <term>original: *Oeconomia*; in theology, this refers to the "Divine Economy," the way God manages or arranges His revelation to humanity</term>, as the Ancients have spoken / that is / through a voluntary representation and depiction; which one may well call the Divine **Shekhinah** <term>original: *Schechinah*; a Hebrew term referring to the dwelling or settling of the divine presence of God</term> / or Indwelling / just as such a word was used by the Ancients / regarding the Indwelling of the Most High in the Tabernacle and in the Temple and among the Prophets.

§. 4. From this it follows / that God the Lord, with this most gracious **Dispensation** <term>original: *Dispensation*; the divine system or arrangement by which God deals with creatures</term> directs Himself according to the creatures / to whom He wishes to communicate Himself / because no creature can in any way direct itself toward Him on account of His incomprehensibility.

§. 5. That this same Revelation is consequently spatial / and occurs at a certain place / because no creature can be everywhere.

That it also §. 6. Occurs with a certain and, without doubt, the most magnificent order / because in God there is no **confusion** <note>original: *Confusion*</note> and disorder / but nothing but pure perfection.

Furthermore, it follows in §. 7. That the most magnificent communication and representation of God occurs at the most magnificent place. But the most magnificent place is / where the most noble creatures (who / because the whole world is full of **Matter** <term>original: *Materii*</term> / just as they cannot live outside the world / so they cannot live without matter /) find the most noble and purest matter; and this place is Heaven / and indeed without doubt that part of Heaven / which has purer matter / than all the **vortices** <term>original: *vortices*; an astronomical term from early modern physics (likely Cartesian) referring to the massive celestial whirlpools of matter that were thought to carry the planets and stars</term> and eddies of the fixed and wandering stars. Therefore, not only did our Savior / when He prayed / look up toward Heaven / Matthew 14:19. Mark 6:41. Chapter 7:34. Luke 9:16. John 17:1. and otherwise, not without cause, had a great fondness for mountains and high places: Matthew 5:1. Mark 3:13. Matthew 14:23. Chapter 15:29. Chapter 17:1. Mark 9:2. Matthew 28:16. Mark 6:46. Luke 6:12. Chapter 9:28. John 6:3, 15. Mark 15:22. John 19:17. And finally, He even desired to be taken up into the heights quite visibly / when He ascended into Heaven / Mark 16:19. Luke 24:51.

# First Stumbling Block.

...to explore the counsels and ways of GOD? It is indeed a difficult thing / just to want to shift and permute <note>original: *permutiren*; to rearrange the order of a set of items</note> the order of the twenty-four letters in the alphabet as often as they allow themselves to be permuted / so that / if there were a thousand times a thousand scribes / and they were to write for a thousand times a thousand years / and indeed each one specifically set down forty permutations or changes of their letter-orders every day / they would still not be able to bring all permutations to an end. Why then would a single poor earthworm <note>A common term of humility in 17th-century devotional writing, emphasizing the lowliness of man compared to the Creator.</note> / given the shortness of his life / indeed in so few weeks / venture to contain and comprehend the infinity of God and his mysteries within such a small pit <note>The original *Grüblin* suggests a small hollow or chamber, but also punningly refers to *Grübeln*, the act of intensive, often circular, human brooding or over-thinking.</note> and the narrow scope of his reason / which cannot be explored in all eternity? Or how dare that same person / with his weak pen / venture to pass a shameful judgment upon that which the Spirit of Rebirth saw in the depth of the Godhead through Jacob Böhme? <note>Jacob Böhme (1575–1624) was a famous German mystic and theologian. His works were often criticized by orthodox clergy for being obscure or heretical.</note> Must not a poor beetle / flying into such light / burn its wings / yes, even itself / and plunge into the abyss? Must not flesh and blood remain behind here? Indeed, no one can explore it / unless it be given to him from above /

->Matthew 16: Therefore let everyone take heed / as I wish to have faithfully warned / against reckless judgment in Divine mysteries.<-

# Second Stone of Stumbling.

### Amaziah’s Remark.

This is a dangerous and unscriptural manner of speaking. Dangerous, because "roaring" is the senseless and irrational voice of a wild lion; and (especially if Amaziah had known from Peter <note>A reference to 1 Peter 5:8, where the devil is compared to a "roaring lion" seeking someone to devour.</note> that the devil is compared to a roaring lion) it is not fitting for the all-wise and Holy GOD. It is also not scriptural, because it is not found in the Book of the Law; and the anointed King and Prophet David uses it in reference to the godless enemies and adversaries of GOD (Psalm 22:14, Psalm 74:4). Amos, however, and several other self-appointed <note>original: *selbst geloffene*; literally 'self-run,' meaning those who took up the prophetic office without being called or ordained by the establishment.</note> younger false prophets, are the first to apply such a monstrous manner of speaking to the pure GOD. Oh, how I fear that the entire prophecy was given to AMOS to disgrace the true God and to exalt another as God.

> Note: Luther himself says in the preface to Isaiah: You should view Isaiah (just like Amos here among the Israelites) among the Jewish people as nothing other than a despised man, indeed like a fool and a madman. For they did not regard him as we do now, but as he himself testifies in Chapter 58:9 <note>Isaiah 58:9 mentions "the pointing of the finger." The author likely also refers to Isaiah 57:4, which mentions sticking out the tongue.</note>, they stuck their tongues out at him, pointed their fingers at him, and considered all his sermons foolishness—except for a very few of God’s children in the crowd, like King Hezekiah, etc. For it was the custom among the people to mock the prophets and consider them insane (2 Kings 9:11).

§. 3. Amos Chapter 1, verses 3, 6, 9, 11, 13. I.

->For three or four transgressions, etc.<-

### Amaziah’s Remark.

This is an absurd and self-contradictory—indeed, a confused and adventurous—manner of speaking: in that he wishes to speak every time of three or four transgressions <term>Laster|Vices or sins. In the biblical book of Amos, the prophet uses the formula "For three transgressions... and for four" to indicate a full measure of sin that triggers divine judgment.</term> for the sake of which the LORD will not show mercy; and yet in the same breath, he speaks of only one transgression.

### §. 4. Amos Chapter 1, verse 1.

This is what Amos etc. has seen etc. two years before the earthquake.

#### Amaziah’s Remark.

By beginning his prophecy with the earthquake right away, he intends to give it a certain weight <term>weight (pondus)</term> and authority, as if providing a sign. But even if the sign should come to pass, one still must not believe him, according to our law cited above, Deuteronomy 13, verses 1, 2, and 3 <note>This biblical passage warns that even if a prophet performs a sign or wonder, they should not be followed if they lead people toward other gods.</note>. Furthermore, as is well known to the scholars in both Jerusalem and Bethel, the earthquake has its natural causes <term>natural causes (causas physicas)</term>.

### §. 5. Amos Chapter 4, verse 1.

Hear this word, you fat cows etc. and say to your masters: "Bring here, let us drink" etc.

#### Amaziah’s Remark.

From this it is clear what he thinks of the Holy Ministry <term>the clerical office (ministerio)</term>: how he seeks to make the ordained priesthood hateful to both the high and the low in the audience <term>the assembly of listeners (auditorio)</term> through his slandering <term>malicious misrepresentation (calumniren)</term> and blasphemies.

### §. 6. Amos. Chapter 8, verse 4.

With this, he takes a jab at taxes and customs <note>The original terms "Schoß" and "Zoll" refer to specific historical land taxes and trade duties.</note>, intending to abolish them and to embitter and incite the people against their superiors.

It is clear from this that he [despises] the ordinances which <meta>catchword: God</meta>

### Amaziah’s Remark.

It is appalling that he decries the Psalter and the songs of David as Epicurean poems <note>Amaziah suggests Amos is reducing sacred music to "Epicurean" verse—poetry intended only for worldly pleasure and indulgence.</note>, as if they were made only for drinking and carousing. In itself, however, this is pure and simple blasphemy against the prophecies of David. Should one not rather wish that all people might prophesy like Moses, and compose and meditate upon spiritual songs like David?

->§. 9. Amos Chapter 9, verse 13.<-

### Amaziah’s Remark.

This is not only contrary to all sober philosophy—for instantaneous motion does not exist <note>original: "non enim datur motus instantaneus"</note>—but the idea that one should plow and harvest at the very same time is nonsensical. Not to mention how absurd it sounds: that one could sow grapes, let alone press them in the wine vat at the same time. With this, he offers us the hollow comfort of a Utopia <term>an imagined perfect society (utopiam)</term> and a lovely Land of Cockaigne <note>The "Schlaur-affen-Land" is a mythical land of plenty in German folklore where food falls into one's mouth and no work is required.</note>, which are nothing but the antics of a Pickel-Hering <note>A "Pickel-Hering" was a popular stock character or clown in 17th-century theater, known for buffoonery.</note>. This is how it sounds and turns out when shoemakers step beyond their lasts <note>A reference to the proverb "Sutor, ne ultra crepidam," meaning one should not comment on matters outside their expertise.</note> and ox-herders and other laypeople or common folk try to speak of philosophical and theological matters.

<note>original Latin: "Contradictoria non possunt simul esse vera, Impossibile enim est idem simul esse & non esse"</note> Contradictory things cannot be true at the same time, for it is impossible for the same thing to both be and not be at once. Now, if the kingdom of Israel is to be utterly destroyed from the face of the earth (for it is clear from Chapter 9, verse 9, that he means Israel—and Israel and Jacob are one and the same, as he himself indicates in Chapter 6, verse 8), how then does that rhyme with these words: *I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob*, Chapter 9, verse 8; and *I will restore the captives of my people Israel*? Especially since, God be praised, we can have all matters of religion—what one should believe, do, and refrain from—as well as all promises and threatened punishments, much more purely, clearly, and perfectly in the Holy Word and infallible yardstick of our Book of the Law <note>Likely referring to the Torah or the Pentateuch</note>, as well as in other spiritual writings of our Rabbis.

# A Heartfelt Warning
## Concerning these rationalizing, fallacious conclusions of the priest Amaziah, alongside the annotations of Holzhausen.

God-loving Reader, I have no need to prove to Christians that the divine book of the Prophet Amos is canonical and inspired by God, and recognized as such by me and all right-believing hearts; rather, this presentation only demonstrates how Reason, when it lacks the <term>Key of David (Schlüssel Davids)</term> <note>A biblical reference to Revelation 3:7, signifying the spiritual authority to understand and open the meaning of the Scriptures</note>, is entirely blind in its zeal for God—so much so that it even murdered His own Son through the Pharisees and tormented His instruments until death. One may look up what Dr. Heinrich Müller reports in his 217th *Hour of Refreshment* <note>Heinrich Müller (1631–1675) was a famous Lutheran devotional writer; his *Erquickstunden* or "Hours of Refreshment" were widely read</note>, as can be seen in the example of Mr. Holzhausen. Indeed, just as the Jews built the tombs of the prophets yet killed and persecuted Christ and His apostles—who followed in the spirit of the prophets—so we now build the tombs of Christ and the apostles while persecuting those who follow in the spirit of Christ and the apostles. This happens simply because we cannot perceive their speech through our reason; instead, what is brought forth by such instruments is a stumbling block to the Jews and foolishness to the pagan naturalists <note>The author is paraphrasing 1 Corinthians 1:23, which describes the Gospel as a "stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles"</note>.

->Therefore take your reason captive under the obedience of Christ.<-
->Amen<-

(17)

<image-desc>A decorative headpiece consisting of five rows of repeating printers' ornaments, including floral patterns, scrollwork, and stylized leaf motifs.</image-desc>

The God-fearing and truth-seeking reader is hereby informed that this consideration <note>original: "Bedencken," a term referring to a formal theological reflection or written opinion.</note> was written by the author only for the instruction of a few good friends in the year of Christ 1675, on December 10th; which was done in haste without the intention <note>original: "Vorsatz."</note> of making it public through open printing. Yet it will hopefully not displease the reader so much, because the desire of many who long for God will be satisfied through this. Should an upright reader find anything unclear due to its brevity, they shall be met at any time with a willing report and further explanation.

But for those who wish to measure everything according to the square <note>original: "Winckelmaaß," a carpenter's tool used here metaphorically to describe a rigid, self-imposed intellectual standard.</note> of their own head, their preconceived opinion <note>original: "Gutdünckel."</note>, and self-invented guideline <note>original: "Richtschnur," literally a plumb line or measuring cord.</note>, and who presumptuously brand as heretical <note>original: "verketzern," which literally means "to treat as a Cathar," the medieval group from which the German word for heretic is derived.</note> (without thorough investigation) everything that seems contrary to their views—for them, we have a rightful Christian compassion, sighing inwardly to God that He might powerfully soften their hard hearts, graciously enlighten them with the light of His eternal truth, and guide and lead them on His divine paths! Grace <note>original: "Gnade."</note> be with us all, Amen!

# Concerning the Sin Against the Holy Spirit.

->§. 1.<-

First, I should cite the various opinions that different theologians and scholars of the Scripture—especially the Church Fathers—have held concerning this sin. However, since doing so would become too extensive, and no one is served by being presented with erroneous opinions when the truth can be had, I rightfully refrain from troubling myself and others in this matter.

§. 2. Especially since God from heaven testified personally of His Son alone: *This is my beloved Son, hear Him* <note>A reference to the Transfiguration (Matthew 17:5).</note>; and since His Son specifically mentions this sin by name, I also rightfully lay only His words as the foundation of this contemplation. I shall pass over other passages of Holy Scripture, as they seem to me to speak more of the *effect* of this sin than of the sin itself. Such sayings of Christ are found in Matthew 12, verses 31 and 32:

> All sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men; but the blasphemy against the Holy Spirit shall not be forgiven unto men. And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him; but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, nor in the world to come.

Mark 3: 28–29:

> Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme; but he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Spirit hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation. Because they said: He hath an unclean spirit.

Luke 12: 10.

> And whosoever shall speak a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him; but unto him that blasphemeth against the Holy Spirit it shall not be forgiven.

§. 4. Regarding common sins, it is not necessary or relevant here to dwell on them; however, the sin against the Son of Man <note>A title used by Jesus to refer to himself in his human capacity.</note> occurs when one takes offense at the outward person of the son of Mary, and neither can nor will regard him as God’s Son and equal to God. This is indeed a great sin, because (if one is serious) there is sufficient instruction to be had regarding it: But yet, because this sin does not go directly or properly into and against the Divine Essence itself, nor does it run against external reason—within which there is nothing that would compel any person to regard another human being as God—therefore, this sin is forgivable <note>original: "vergeblich," which in this context means pardonable or capable of being forgiven.</note>.

§. 5. Therefore, although the Jews and Turks <note>In the 17th and 18th centuries, "Turks" was the standard European term for Muslims.</note> commit this sin daily, for that reason the door of grace—should they only desire it—is not closed to them.

§. 6. However, that Christ says in Mark that blasphemy against God shall indeed be forgiven, but not blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, happens because a blasphemy against God can indeed occur where the one committing it does not recognize it as such, or otherwise does it out of a clouded mind <note>original: "Verstossung des Gemüths," referring to a state of mental confusion, distress, or lack of spiritual clarity.</note>, and therefore does not run against God with their whole will; otherwise, it would not be possible to find a distinction between blasphemy against God and blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, as is well known.

§. 7. But to examine the sin against the Holy Spirit quite distinctly from other sins based on the aforementioned foundation, one must well consider: (1) Who the Holy Spirit is? (2) How one sins against Him? (3) Why this sin, above all others, is held by Christ to be unforgivable?

§. 8. Out of a love for brevity, I refrain from citing things concerning God the Holy Spirit which are undisputed in the Church of God, or which otherwise do not properly belong to the treatment of this current controversial matter; this I have deemed necessary to add as a condition.

### Third Stumbling Block

The Supreme Teacher, Judge, Governor, and Disciplinarian of the holy Christian Church is He who teaches, reminds, exhorts, and drives every person toward that which is good, holy, pleasing to God, and useful to everyone. He does this not only externally through the **Preaching Office** <note>original: "Predigt-Ampt," referring to the formal role of clergy and the delivery of sermons.</note> but also through His internal testimony. He also terrifies, warns, and punishes everyone—not only externally through the preaching office, but also internally in the **conscience**, where He has His judgment seat—against all evil. God the Holy Spirit performs this work in all people, without exception, as the undeniable experience of all clearly proves.

§. 10. And it is the earnest will of God the Holy Spirit that no human soul withdraws itself from such judgment, at the risk of losing His grace and their salvation. No one should contradict His verdict, but rather all should obediently submit to Him and His court and judgment. By doing so, they would be led on a level path, preserved from all error, confirmed in all that is good, and sealed for eternal life.

§. 11. To this end, God the Holy Spirit has not relied solely on His own word and testimony in His Church—both the public testimony found in the **Scriptures** and the personal testimony through the **conscience**. Rather, He has also accepted and ordained the Holy Preaching Office to serve as co-witnesses, so that the people of the Lord might be instructed all the more correctly and in the best possible way.

§. 12. However, this is only to the extent that the *Ministry* <note>original Latin: "Ministerium," referring here to the body of clergy or the clerical estate.</note> does not treat such an office of the Spirit as a personal possession <note>original: "Eigenthumb," implying that ministers should not claim the power of the Spirit as their own property or right.</note>, desiring to rule over others. Instead, they must look solely to the voice of the highest Judge of the Church in all things and not deviate in the slightest from His line of judgment. Rather, it should always be said: **"It has pleased the Holy Spirit and us."** <note>original Latin reference: *Acts 15:28*.</note> Only then is it rightly said: **"whoever hears you, hears me."** <note>original Latin reference: *Luke 10:16*.</note>

§. 13. It can happen, however, as has often occurred, that one or many use the preaching office as a personal possession. They strut about in it, seeking not God's honor or the edification of people in the truth, but rather seeking their own interests. They pass off their own views as God's office and thus, through their own works, wit, and prestige, they overstep the office of the Holy Spirit. In doing so, they lead themselves and others away from God and the internal life, directing them toward themselves and external matters, to the eternal harm of both themselves and their listeners.

### Third Stumbling Block

§. 14. Since God takes no pleasure in the destruction of anyone, the Holy Spirit stands against those leaders of the Church who corrupt their ways. He opposes them both in their own conscience and through His "instruments"—whether these messengers are chosen through the regular church order or through extraordinary means. He punishes them for their straying, points them back to the path from which they have deviated, and—so that they might have no excuse—He equips these **legates** <note>original: "Legaten," meaning envoys or representatives sent on a specific mission.</note> with sufficient **criteria** <note>original: "Criteriis," meaning distinguishing marks or proofs of divine authority.</note> and signs.

§. 15. In such instances, these leaders should not stubbornly resist the testimony of the Holy Spirit in their conscience, nor His messengers and servants in His role as Judge. Instead, they should test these messengers—rigorously, yet with humility and gentleness. Upon finding that the messengers are from God and speak the truth, the leaders should fall on their faces, give God the glory, and allow themselves to be set right.

§. 16. Often, however, the opposite occurs. Because they now treat the office of the Spirit as their own personal property and rule within it—and because it feels so good to the "outer man" and the people are content with it in their **sleepiness** <note>original: "Schläfferigkeit," referring to a state of spiritual lethargy or indifference among the congregation.</note> (as seen in Jeremiah 5:31)—they are unwilling to leave the sins in which they find themselves so comfortable. Therefore, when God the Holy Spirit tries to correct them, they struggle against Him. They pit themselves and their own human "judgment" against the Judge (the Holy Spirit) and His instruments. They do this to such an extent that they blaspheme even against their own conscience, against Christian love, and against all reason, passing devilish judgments on what is actually the true work of God the Holy Spirit.

§. 17. This is precisely the **Sin against the Holy Spirit** <term>original: "Sünde in den heil. Geist." In theology, this is the "unpardonable sin," defined here not just as an error, but as a deliberate, judicial rejection of the Spirit's corrective office.</term> of which Christ speaks in the cited passages. It bears this name because it specifically attacks the unique character of the Holy Spirit: namely, His office as Teacher and Judge.

§. 18. That this is the case is shown so clearly by Christ Himself through the example of the **Pharisees** <note>A prominent Jewish sect in the New Testament; the author uses them as the primary historical example of those who consciously rejected divine truth to protect their own status.</note> that every Christian can apply these points for themselves.

§. 19. From this, it becomes especially clear that committing this sin does not necessarily require a prior "sufficient knowledge of the truth." Such knowledge was not found among the Pharisees, as Peter and Paul testify (Acts 3:17; 1 Corinthians 2:8), stating that they did not recognize Christ, for had they known Him, they would not have crucified the Lord of Glory. Rather, it is enough if such people, in their formal proceedings, act "judicially" against the Holy Spirit's verdict—acting against conscience, Christian love, and natural reason.

§. 20. And although one might object with what **Nicodemus** mentions in **John 3:2**, and likewise what the disciples of the **Pharisees** bring forward in **Matthew 22:16**, all of this signifies nothing. Rather, the former confirms my assertion and teaches us to distinguish between the knowledge of the conscience and that of the outer reason or **opinion**. Their conscience surely told them (not necessarily that **Jesus** was the Messiah) but that he was a teacher come from **God**, for no one could do the signs that he did unless **God** were with him. Others also could have done these signs according to their understanding, had **God** been with them. But according to the knowledge of outer reason, they believed they had significant reasons not to take him for the Messiah; they also believed that the Scripture was strongly on their side because **Jesus** was not born in **Bethlehem**, according to the Scripture, but in **Nazareth**, contrary to the Scripture. <note>The author refers to the common biblical debate where skeptics rejected Jesus because they believed he was from Nazareth, overlooking his birth in Bethlehem as prophesied in Micah 5:2.</note> Upon this they insist and boast, as if on an irrefutable ground, as can be seen in **John 7:41**. The other reason requires no answer.

§. 21. It also seems to have little merit when some claim that this sin is unforgivable only because such a sinner stubbornly and persistently rejects the means of conversion.

§. 22. Rather, the matter stands thus: Because such a person denies, blasphemes, and condemns the testimony of the Holy Spirit within him and outside him (through which every person is drawn by **God** into **God**, indeed is attached and bound to **God**), and rebels against **God** the Holy Spirit and His judgments no differently than **Absalom** did against **David** <note>Absalom was the son of King David who led a famous rebellion against his father, symbolizing a betrayal of the closest possible bond.</note> (even if he does not recognize or confess it), by this very act he has torn the divine bond within himself and thus completely broken away from **God**. Therefore, just as it is in **natural matters**, so it is in **divine matters** regarding such a person: **there is no return from deprivation to possession.** <note>original: "à Privatione ad habitum non datur regreſſus." This is a philosophical principle suggesting that once a fundamental spiritual capacity is completely destroyed, it cannot be naturally restored.</note>

§. 23. Yet it is not denied that he who sins, as **Thummius** <note>Theodor Thumm (1586–1630), a prominent Lutheran theologian known for his works on Christology and sin.</note> **defines it**, has truly committed this sin. However, to become guilty of this sin, it is not necessary that all of this must have been actually committed beforehand; for otherwise the sin would become too unrecognizable and not at all consistent with the example given by **Christ** himself—which, without any doubt, **Satan** would very well tolerate...

...be forgiven, because thus sin is less feared, and even less avoided, but rather is committed more boldly. It is, however, enough that when the sin has already been committed, all these enormities and improprieties—as the inevitable fruits of a rotten tree—occur forcefully as opportunities arise.

§. 24. Therefore, the sin is most suitably described as follows: The **sin against the Holy Spirit** is a—primarily by the leaders of the churches—haughty, willful, and judicial contradiction, blasphemy, and condemnation of the office, power, and working of **God the Holy Spirit**, through which He seeks to restore those who have strayed from the truth. This occurs against the testimony of one's own conscience, against the love of **Christ**, and natural equity <note>or "fairness"</note>, whereby such a person breaks away from the drawing of **God**, and thus from **God** Himself, and thereby loses all further access to grace and conversion. Thus (it seems to me) the definition and the thing defined <note>The author uses the logical terms "definition" and "definitum" to show how his description matches the actual occurrence.</note> agree perfectly in the example of the **Pharisees** given by **Christ** Himself.

§. 25. This terrifying sin arises, like almost all others, primarily from wretched pride, accompanied by the vices that **Christ** attributes to the **Pharisees** in **Matthew 23**.

§. 26. To which sins they were (unrecognized) so devoted that they did not even think of any conversion, but relying on their external office and divine service, they wished to remain entirely unmastered before the judgment of the **Holy Spirit** and His instruments. Therefore, **God the Lord** sent them powerful delusions, so that they (gathered together as a body <note>original: "collegialiter versammlet," referring to their meeting as a formal council or college</note>) not only took a completely false proposition for certain truth but also established it as their foundation without any investigation. From this, they dared to judicially oppose the Spirit of Grace, both in His instruments and in His judgment—yet against conscience, love, and equity—and believed themselves compelled to hold His proven divine miracles in suspicion, and even to proclaim them as devilish.

### Third Stumbling Block.

§. 27. One such false proposition was, among others: That Christ was not born in Bethlehem, but in Nazareth; **therefore** <note>original Latin: "Ergò"</note> he could not be the Messiah, and thus his miracles were suspicious. This, although it was entirely false, they nevertheless held—and this is most remarkable for such learned people—**collegially** <note>original Latin: "collegialiter," meaning acting as a formal body or assembly</note> to be absolutely certain.

§. 28. By this path, they fell into the most terrifying sin, yet remained so insensitive to it that they preferred themselves above all others and considered themselves alone to be God’s dear children; meanwhile, they fiercely persecuted and outlawed the true children of God, as if acting out of divine zeal.

§. 29. Oh! That we would be wiser today, and that no one would fall into the same **example** of unbelief!

§. 30. Oh! That all leaders of the churches would learn that they, above others, are in danger because of this cruel sin; yet others should also take heed!

§. 31. Let all, however, earnestly guard themselves against wretched **pride** <term>pride: "Hoffart," an archaic German term for a haughty, arrogant, or boastful spirit that seeks status over others</term> and the sins following from it; instead, let them zealously observe Christ’s teaching and life in *Matthew* 5, 6, and 7, and seek to practice them faithfully.

§. 32. Also, let them be heartily warned not to ground themselves **collegially** <note>that is, as a group or committee</note> upon any proposition before the opposing side has been heard in an orderly, rational, friendly, Christianly-proper, and sufficient manner.

§. 33. And let no one imagine that he does not err, or that he is entirely certain of the matter, but rather consider: since this delusion has so dangerously deceived some, it is not impossible for the same to happen to him.

§. 34. Which would, without doubt, happen to very many, if they only took to heart more often this terrifying **verdict** <note>original Latin: "Sentenz"</note> of Christ, and if no one, out of false confidence in himself, wished to consider it impossible to be swallowed up in this abyss.

§. 35. This is especially necessary in the present time, when so many highly wonderful works bear powerful witness that God from heaven accuses His people—who are called Christians—and their leaders of straying, and calls them to recognition <note>or "acknowledgment of the truth"</note> through His judgments and witnesses.

### Third Stumbling Block.

§. 36. He also provides them with such undeniable divine signs <note>original: "Merckzeichen"</note> that can be sufficient to convince all consciences, even though external reason still believes it has much to complain about against them.

§. 37. Thus, it can easily happen today that the leaders of the churches, stumbling over these persons, might not only push ahead of the judgment of God the Holy Spirit through their prejudice, but might even blaspheme and condemn such a judgment of the Holy Spirit over themselves and His people, unless they guard themselves diligently and remain watchful.

§. 38. Such prejudices today are: (1) Our church alone is the purest; therefore no one is to be heard or tolerated unless they are a member of our church. (2) God the Lord never indicates His will **immediately** <term>immediately: "Immediate," referring to direct revelation from God to an individual without the mediation of the church or scripture</term> or **extraordinarily**; therefore no one is to be heard who is called in any way other than the **ordinary** <term>ordinary: "Ordinarie," referring to the standard institutional process of appointing clergy</term> way. §. 39. However, whichever leader of the church, building upon these prejudices, sets himself against the holy working of God the Holy Spirit, and on this basis denies, blasphemes, and condemns such a work, he will act no more wisely than the Pharisees. Based on the premise that "no prophet arises out of Galilee," they concluded that Christ could not be the Messiah; therefore, even His undeniable divine miracles did not move them.

§. 40. Those who now dare to do so should know that no one will guarantee that they are not thereby committing this most terrifying sin <note>referring to the unforgivable sin against the Holy Spirit</note>.

§. 41. Because it is undeniable that such a person proves himself entirely similar to the example of the Pharisees, whom Christ Himself presented as the example for this sin; therefore, the **thing being defined** <note>original Latin: "Definitum"</note> cannot well be denied when the **definition** <note>original Latin: "Definition"</note> itself is so clearly evident.

§. 42. This I have wished to sketch as briefly as possible, from a Christian and impartial spirit, for the sake of no one’s favor or offense, but for the glory of God alone, for the service of my neighbor, and for my own practice.

### The Third Stumbling Block.

§. 43. However, since no one is unaware of Satan’s cunning—how he often tends to make great sins appear small and small ones appear large—it is only right to counter the spiritual trial <note>original: "Anfechtung," a Lutheran term for deep spiritual distress or the feeling of being under assault by doubt and despair</note> that he might push into weak <note>original: "blöde," meaning timid or fragile rather than unintelligent</note> hearts, as if they were guilty of this sin.

§. 44. Firstly, such a person can conclude from this very trial that he is not guilty of this sin. For whoever has actually committed this sin remains without such spiritual distress; indeed, he is so proud and angry that he cares for no one. In all his malice, he considers God as nothing; he continues in his ways forever, and God’s judgments are far from him.

§. 45. Furthermore, if such an afflicted person finds within himself even a single, deeply hidden desire <note>original: "Wille"</note> that longs for God’s mercy in repentance, then it is certain that he is not yet (fully) guilty of this sin and has not been entirely cut off from God. For this desire does not come from human nature, but is the certain drawing of the Father to the Son. Therefore, let no one hold back, but as soon as the desire for God’s mercy is stirred, let him look within and come immediately, like the Prodigal Son to his father; then the grace of the Heavenly Father will surely be open to him again. Luke 15.

§. 46. Even if such an afflicted person has imagined this sin all too strongly, and the terrifying words of Christ are pressed hard upon him—especially since one reads in Numbers 23:19: *God is not a man, that He should lie, nor a son of man, that He should repent; should He say something and not do it?*—one should nevertheless demonstrate <note>original: "remonstriren"</note> to him that *mercy triumphs over judgment.* James 2:13 <note>The OCR lists John 2:13, but the author is quoting James 2:13</note>. Therefore, His severity <note>original: "Ernsthafftigkeit"</note> has often spoken what His mercy has later softened. For example <note>original: "e. g."</note>, in Matthew 15, He says: *I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel,* and yet He helps that very woman against whom He spoke those words. In Matthew 10:5, He forbids preaching to the Gentiles and Samaritans, and yet how graciously He deals with the Gentile Gadarenes <note>original: "Gergesenern"</note> in Matthew 8:28, and the Samaritans in John 4.

### CHAPTER I.

# In which Mr. **Holz-Hausen** sets forth some general remarks regarding why one must be on guard against **Jacob Boehme’s** writings.

## The First **Holz-Hausen** Remark.

Since we are warned in Holy Scripture against false prophets and their great hypocrisy and boasting; we do right, and are even duty-bound to do so, as often as something new in matters of religion is presented to us—of which nothing has been heard in Christendom until now—that we do not rush headlong and accept it as something good, but first test it well according to Holy Scripture. This is especially true for those who hold the teaching office <term>Lehrambt</term> <note>The official position of an ordained minister or theologian responsible for the spiritual oversight of a congregation.</note> and are meant to warn others against false doctrine. Since in this century <note>original: "Seculo"</note> so much fuss has been made by some regarding Boehme's writings, and since they are found to be well-suited to prepare the minds of inquisitive people for Quakerism <term>Quäckerey</term> <note>A term used by 17th-century orthodox theologians to categorize various "enthusiastic" or mystical sects, including the Quakers, whom they viewed as a threat to organized church structure.</note>, our listeners are also rightly warned against them.

## Their Christian Investigation.

Since you also, however, my dear Mr. **Holz-Hausen**, are warned in Holy Scripture against wicked judging and condemning of your neighbor, so that you might not be judged and condemned (Matthew 7:1; Romans 2:1-9), and against quenching the spirit in a divine instrument <note>The author here suggests that Jacob Boehme might be a "divine instrument" or vessel for God’s word, and warns Holtzhausen not to dismiss him too quickly.</note> (1 Thessalonians 5:19), so

## The Second Holtzhausen Remark.

Because Boehme’s writings are so numerous that they make a book almost twice as large as the entire Holy Scripture, and since we already have as many soul-saving mysteries of faith in the Holy Scripture as are necessary for salvation; therefore, we should not take the precious time away from reading the Holy Scripture—of which we are certain that it is inspired by the Holy Spirit—and apply it to reading such an extensive and uncertain book. # Christian Investigation of the 5th

Christ the **Lord** has indeed taught us in Holy Scripture that false prophets come to us in sheep’s clothing on the outside (but not on the inside), whereas inwardly they are ravenous wolves (Matthew 7:15); that they keep their cups and dishes clean on the outside (not on the inside), but inwardly are full of robbery and gluttony; that they are like whitewashed tombs, which appear beautiful on the outside (not on the inside), but are full of bones of the dead and all filth on the inside (Matthew 23:25-27). - 2. That Satan himself could disguise or transform himself into an angel of light, both inwardly and outwardly. This is not only a completely new and unheard-of way of speaking, but also a monstrous doctrine running against **God** and nature, where King Lucifer is so courted that the angelic form of light is ascribed to him not only outwardly, but also internally again. If Mr. Holzhausen had allowed himself to be led into the "Book of Nature" <note>A common concept in mystical theology where the physical world is seen as a secondary "scripture" that reveals divine truths through the properties of matter.</note> by the Holy Spirit along with Jacob Böhme and had observed the ores, stones, and metals, he would have been convinced of something else. For example: where dark lead is not only gilded on the outside with gold leaf, but is also converted into gold in its inner essence and center, then the lead would truly be transmuted <note>The author uses the alchemical term "transmutirt" to argue that a change in "inner essence" constitutes a change in the thing itself.</note> into gold, and would therefore be true gold. 

Likewise, if Satan himself did not only take on the external form of an angel of light, but were also transformed into it inwardly, he would be able to lay aside his devilish nature—indeed, would have *de facto* laid it aside—insofar as Mr. Holzhausen ascribes such inward and outward transformation to him in matters that have already occurred. To be sure, Satan can objectively present his deceptions to others externally, and especially blind the senses of the unbelieving, but this little verse is not speaking of that; rather, it speaks subjectively of Satan himself: that he disguises himself as an angel of light, or more reflectively in the original text: "he himself is transformed" <note>original Greek: "μετασχηματίζεται αυτός" (metaschēmatizetai autos). # Holzhausen Notes. Chapter I.

Just as the preceding context previously speaks of the false apostles—how they (through Satan's cunning) are transformed into apostles of Christ—so now this verse proceeds, as if *by some digression* <note>original Latin: "per aliquam digressionem"</note>, to Satan in and of himself, in *opposition* <note>original Latin: "oppositione"</note> or contrast to what occurs with the false prophets. ## The Seventh Remark by Holtzhausen.

These admirers of **Böhme** attribute all his writings entirely to the **Holy Spirit** as His own work—and even the specific order in which the writings followed one another (see pages 12 and 14 in the admirers' preface). But another particular admirer, **Hans Dietrich Thresch**, says in his letters—which are printed at the end of the *Aurora*—that **Jacob Böhme** judged this first writing of his, the *Aurora*, as an "imperfect birth." <note>Böhme wrote *Aurora* in 1612; it was famously seized by authorities before it was finished.</note> He constantly pleaded for people to hold back on this first birth, because there were many things in it that could conflict with his other writings and make the entire body of work appear suspicious.

This judgment by **Böhme** is true; however, it does not match the boastful praise claiming that his writing is such a pure work of the **Holy Spirit**, right down to the order of publication. If the **Holy Spirit** had intended such an order—that this *Aurora* should be the first book, just as the day rises with the dawn—then **Jacob Böhme** should not have been afraid to let this book come forth first. But it seems **Jacob Böhme** "smelled a rat" <note>original: *den Braten gerochen*, literally "smelled the roast," a German idiom for sensing trouble or a hidden motive.</note> or was warned by others to hold this book back for a while until his other writings had gained proper credit. For it is true, as **Jacob Böhme** himself judged: from this *Aurora* one naturally develops a disgust, loathing, and horror for all his other writings. Therefore, **God** may have arranged it through a special <term>Providence</term> <note>The protective care of God as a spiritual power steering human history.</note> so that by his first book—as if by a gruesome <term>Aurora</term> <note>original: *Morgenröhte*. The title of Böhme's first book, *Aurora*, is Latin for "dawn."</note> or morning-dawn—we should recognize and perceive what a gruesome day would follow such a gruesome dawn in **Böhme’s** writings.

<meta>This page continues the critique of rigid academic philosophy from the previous section. ### Holzhausen's Preface to Chapter II.

The "Divine Plato" <note>original: "Divinus plato"</note>—so named because of his considerable insight into the **mental world** <note>original Latin: "mundum mentalem," referring to the realm of ideas or spiritual reality.</note> or the angelic realm—says as a pagan: "To investigate God is most difficult; to declare Him to the masses is impossible." <note>original Latin: "Deum investigare difficillimum, in vulgus enunciare impossibile."</note> That is: to search for God is hard, and to express Him to the common people is impossible. Furthermore, the Holy Church Father **Augustine** also says: "God is thought more truly than He is spoken, and He exists more truly than He is thought." <note>original Latin: "veriùs cogitatur Deus, quám dicitur, & veriùs est quàm cogitatur."</note> This means: God is more profoundly or properly contemplated inwardly than He is expressed by the tongue, and He is more truly Himself in His own being than He can ever be contemplated.

Therefore, the God-enlightened **Jacob Böhme**, in his work *Aurora*, indicates this many, many times, and specifically says: "Indeed, if I had an angelic tongue and you had an angelic understanding, we might speak of it beautifully; but as it is, only the spirit sees it, and the tongue cannot lift it up <note>i.e., express or exalt the mystery</note>; for I can use no other words than the words of this world. However, if only the Holy Spirit is within you, then your soul will surely grasp it." (See pages 95–96 of the old edition, or Chapter 4, verse 29 in the new edition of his *Aurora*). 

It therefore runs against both reason and love when someone chooses to blaspheme such divine things because of the unlearned manner of speaking <note>Böhme was a self-taught shoemaker and often used non-academic, "unlearned" language.</note> about such high mysteries—mysteries which even no learned tongue is capable of expressing skillfully. This is especially true regarding that book <note>The *Aurora*.</note> which he wrote simply for his own **private memorandum** <note>original Latin: "in privato"</note> and never intended to make public, as is clear and evident in his aforementioned letters. 

If, instead of the **Porphyrian Tree in the pagan philosophy of the Peripatetics** <note>The "Arbor Porphyriana" is a traditional logical diagram used to categorize reality, favored by the "Peripatetics" or followers of Aristotle.</note>, one were instead to practice the deepest true humility in the contemplation of the **Sephirotic Tree in the divine theology of the Hebrews** <note>The "Arbor Sephirotica" refers to the Tree of Life in Jewish Kabbalah, representing the ten attributes or emanations of God.</note>—and if one did not bolt the gates and bars against the inner light of grace from the Holy Spirit through blasphemy and obstinacy—a more wholesome knowledge of God would soon follow. Or, if the Holy Apostle Peter’s "Christian Tree" with its branches were allowed to stand, then the fruits of knowledge would also follow, according to 2 Peter 1:5, 6, 7, 8. <note>This passage in the Bible lists a "chain" of virtues—faith, virtue, knowledge, self-control, etc.—which the author envisions as branches of a tree.</note>

## Christian Investigation of the Same.

That the commentator <note>Referring to the critic Holzhausen.</note> has judged the late Böhme <term>precipitantly</term> <note>original: *præcipitanter*; acting with extreme haste and without due reflection.</note> without thought, and thus irresponsibly, and has condemned him against all love, also appears here from the first line, which has no complete sense or meaning, and clearly testifies that it was written down with pure precipitancy. There are mainly four points which Mr. Holzhausen here endeavors to censure and bring into suspicion.

The **first** is, that Lucifer is numbered among the **seven spirits of God**.

The **second**, that he frequently calls him a **Lord**.

The **third**, that he speaks against the common way of speaking: that the **angels are made out of the Father**, and [claims] it should much rather be called **created** or **made by God**.

The **fourth**, that he teaches that the angels, and thus also Lucifer, were **created before the time of the world**, and are thus **eternal spirits**.

...assert: that the angels, as creatures, are equally eternal with the Godhead in their creaturely nature, because he reports: The angels, and thus also Lucifer, were created before the time of the world, and *consequently* <note>original: *Consequenter*</note> from eternity. The second had its beginning, and is thus not from eternity like **God**; but it also remains in eternity, though it took its beginning before the visible material world, which only followed after the former. Therefore, Böhme speaks rightly: their beginning was before the time of the (understand: visible material) world.

This third visible world, as it is transitory and will—along with the visible heaven and earth—be made free again from the "service of vanity" to which it is subject; so it also received the beginning of its creation and time after that other world.

### Holtzhausen’s Annotations on Chapter II.

Source-spirits <note>original: *Quell-Geister*; in the mysticism of Jakob Böhme, these are the seven fundamental properties or "fountains" of divine power that form all reality.</note> according to their properties in magnificent pomp and order, *represented* and revealed the uncreated **GOD** in a creaturely way, as was already mentioned above.

(4) So we also know from the *Kabbalah* and Holy Scripture—and it is proven through this *representation* and revelation of God in the creaturely state—how unspeakably greater the power, strength, authority, and effect of this creaturely Divinity or divine likeness is than our reason (which is ordered within this third material world) can believe or comprehend. These angelic spirits can *produce* powerful things, wonders, and supersensory works within nature and creation, and work astonishing changes in nature through their divine powers.

(5) Furthermore, we can certainly judge from this that, although the *Archetypal World* <note>original: *Mundus Archetypus*; the divine blueprint or realm of ideas in God's mind.</note> in its central essence, with its uncreated sevenfold *emanation*, is and remains the *most simple essence* <note>original: *essentia simplicissima*; a theological concept meaning that God is not composed of different parts but is a perfect unity.</note>, a most singular and subtle being; yet, on the other hand—no matter how high it may be—such a high degree of *simplicity* can never exist in any creature, precisely because of its creaturely nature, as it exists in the pure, uncreated Godhead. Therefore, the Angelic World, when compared to the Godhead (not as they speak in the schools through *physical composition* <note>original: *per compositionem physic.*</note> or *by way of supposition* <note>original: *per modum suppositionis*</note>, but only *comparatively*), is nothing else than as the body is to the soul and spirit which governs the body. It is thus rightly called **God’s** Body—not indeed *by way of physical informing* <note>original: *per modum informationis physicæ*; a scholastic term for how a soul gives form and life to matter</note>, but through *efficiency* <note>original: *efficientiæ*; meaning the power to act or produce an effect</note>. This is just as *Jacob Böhme* <note>A famous 17th-century German mystic and master of theosophy whose work deeply influenced this text.</note>, when he speaks of the Angelic World and its spiritual inhabitants, gives the angels the name of "corporeality." However, this is not in the manner of our material flesh; rather, he calls the body a <term>Power-Body: A spiritual or "light" body composed of divine energy and strength rather than heavy, physical matter.</term> and acknowledges that he must speak only by way of likeness, in the way that a fleshy tongue can express things with words of this material third world. This is due to a lack of angelic tongues and the lack of angelic hearing among the listeners—which should be carefully noted for future Holtzhausen annotations.

# Holtzhausen. Remark on Chapter II.

Seventhly, through this Boehmian Mystery <note>Referring to the mystical philosophy of Jacob Böhme (1575–1624), who believed the physical world was created out of a "shattered" spiritual realm.</note> of the infection of the earth, the difficulty regarding the Tree of Temptation <note>The Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil.</note> is resolved, where a weak-believer might fall into the temptation of thinking: How? How then did the knowledge of Good and Evil come to that same tree, if God created everything good? Or did God not see that it would cost so many thousands of poor souls? 

Thus one sees clearly that God did not create the evil, but rather it came into this world through the devil's envy; one sees then that the Tree of Temptation took its first origin from Satan's evil infection—which had mixed itself in alongside the good—and not from the good God. One sees that God's prohibition was such a serious matter that it should be regarded more as a true fatherly warning than as something God did to tempt him. For God tempts no one to evil, but each one is tempted when he is incited and lured by his own lust; thereafter, when lust has conceived, it gives birth to sin. <margin>James 1:13, 14, 15.</margin> 

Thus one sees that something lust-inciting and easily infecting must have previously crept into the Salniter <term>Salniter: A technical term used by Jacob Böhme to describe the "living salts" or the essential, active forces of Nature; it is the spiritual "soil" from which all things grow.</term> or nature from which Adam was created, rather than falling into the troublesome thoughts that God Himself caused the evil in the Tree of Temptation. Rather, He made everything good by turning the evil—through His all-wise direction <note>original: *Direction*</note> and correction <note>original: *Correction*</note>—into something good.

Finally, the devilish infection of the Earth is also evident from the approaching Last Judgment; there, a separation and division will occur—not only of the godly and evil people—but also the complete judgment over the Devil and his angels, along with a cleansing of Heaven and Earth. The Devil, who at his fall was cast upon the Earth and bound with chains of darkness, shall finally be cast from there into the fiery pit and sulfur. However, the infected Earth, which this *Abaddon*, *Apollyon*, or Destroyer <note>Biblical names from Revelation 9:11 for the angel of the bottomless pit.</note> had so infected at his fall with his serpent-seed and poison, will not indeed be annihilated, but renewed and purified by fire. In this same way, Doctor Luther speaks:

> “ Since the heavens shall not remain, much
> “ less the Earth. Therefore all creatures,
> “ even the heavens, shall be transformed;
> “ not perish and become nothing, but be renewed.

See the third section of *Luther Revived, Title XXXI: On Heaven, page 257.* <note>Referencing a collection of Martin Luther's writings.</note> Thus, it is no annihilation <note>original: *Annihilatio*</note>, but as the Evangelists speak, a transition <note>original: *Transitus*</note> of Heaven and Earth through the fire of purification. This concept is also found by Mr. Thomasius <note>Christian Thomasius (1655–1728), a famous German philosopher and jurist.</note> among the Stoics <note>An ancient Greek school of philosophy that believed the universe is periodically destroyed by fire and then reborn.</note> in their "burning of the world" <note>original: *exustione mundi*</note>; therefore, the fleeing of the previous Earth and the sight of a new Heaven and a new Earth—where the former shall no longer be remembered—does not imply a substantial destruction <note>original: *substantialem interitum*</note> or a substantial new creation. Instead, it signifies a renewal and purification <note>original: *renovationem u. repurgationē*</note>, as it would run contrary to divine omnipotence, wisdom, and goodness if one were to establish its total annihilation. For if God were to annihilate the substances themselves—which are, after all, inherently good both metaphysically and physically <note>original: *Metaphysicè* and *Physicè*</note>—it would mean He either could not or would not preserve them. The former would be a prejudice against His infinite power and wisdom; the latter would go against His inexhaustible goodness and unchangeability.

Therefore, in the remaining parts, we can avoid all long-windedness.

## Holtzhausen’s Remark

1. Böhme confuses visible and invisible creatures—namely, the angels and humans.

2. The Scripture clearly shows that the angels are spirits, according to Hebrews 1: *Are they not all ministering spirits?* <note>Hebrews 1:14</note>. To say that Lucifer and Adam were both made from one <term>Salniter</term> <note>original: *Salniter*; in Böhme's chemistry-inspired theology, this refers to "sal-nitrum," a divine, explosive substance or "universal seed" from which the powers of nature are formed</note> is also not spoken according to the Scriptures.

4. Böhme intends to prove the physical human form of the angels according to their essence by the fact that the angels here on earth have never revealed themselves to humans in any form other than a human one. However, just as the <term>Holy Spirit</term> does not possess a physical dove-like form according to His essence simply because He appeared in one; so it does not follow from such appearances of angels in human form that the angels actually possess a human form. Furthermore, it is not true that the angels have appeared in no other form than that of a human. ### Christian Investigation of the Same.

Regarding the 1st point of this remark: that Böhme confuses visible and invisible creatures—namely, the angels and humans. To this, I answer **NO**; for when he says that angels and humans have **one image**, he is not speaking of the outer person, but of the inner person, who is created after God’s image in holiness and righteousness, according to Ephesians 4:24. As he clearly says in the passage cited <note>original: *loco citato*</note>: "just as a human is created in God's image and likeness, so too are the angels," etc. Is that then false? For the rest, he conversely speaks clearly and distinctly: "every angel is fashioned together out of all the powers of God"—**Note:** not with flesh and blood, but out of divine power. This is surely distinguished clearly enough. One should also read what he writes on page 399: "and therefore we cannot see the angels in our outermost birth <note>original: *eussersten Gebuhrt*; in Böhme’s terminology, 'birth' refers to a state of being or a level of manifestation. The 'outermost birth' is the physical, material world we perceive with our five senses</note>, and the angels also cannot dwell with us in the outermost birth of this world; however, in the innermost birth, they do dwell with us," etc.

Regarding the 2nd point, the verses that Holzhausen wants to cite from Hebrews 1 and 2 and Luke 24 against Jacob Böhme: these are not against him, as can be seen from the already answered first point, since Böhme himself makes exactly this distinction there. ## Holzhausen’s Note.

Here, the absolute immortality of the angels is made equal to the absolute immortality of God; also, the Divine Essence is mixed into the essence of the angels, which is against Holy Scripture.

## Christian Investigation of the same.

Jacob Böhme can never seem to satisfy Mr. Holzhausen; just before, he wanted to force the point that Jacob Böhme supposedly made the strong angels into fragile flesh and blood; but now (which is a clear proof against him that they are endowed with a **power-body** <note>original: *Krafft-Leib*</note> and not with a **material body**, and thus are rather of a **spiritual-creaturely substance**), he is nonetheless displeased by the indestructibility of angelic substances as well. Yet Böhme only means that just as there is no one outside of the Godhead who could destroy it—much less God Himself—so also there is nothing outside of GOD that could destroy an angel, much less the angel destroy itself. If that is false, then I demand that the creature be specified which could **annihilate** an angel. For whether GOD Himself, according to His **absolute power** <note>original: *potentia absoluta*; a theological term referring to God's ability to do anything that does not involve a logical contradiction</note>, could not do so, Böhme has not said here, although something more might be said on this, in that they became creaturely immediately out of the uncreated GOD.

But that Böhme mixes the (understand: uncreated) Essence of the Godhead into the (creaturely) essence of the angels, Holzhausen will never be able to prove from J. Böhme in all eternity. However, he can prove that the angel was created and made creaturely out of the uncreated **Groundless** <note>original: *Ungrund*; a central concept in Böhme's philosophy referring to the absolute, undifferentiated source or "abyss" from which all existence and the Godhead itself emerges</note> of the Godhead; which is, however, quite another thing, and has been sufficiently proven above from the Holy Scripture and the **ancient theology of the Hebrews**; as Jacob Böhme also says:

> " GOD, as in His **Trinity**, is unchangeable; everything that is in **Heaven** and on **Earth**, and above the Earth, has its source and origin from the **power** that proceeds from GOD. page 66.

...be **truly distinguished in a Thomistic sense** <note>original: *Thomisticè realiter distinguirt* — referring to the school of Thomas Aquinas, which argued that the faculties of the soul are distinct from its essence.</note>; in which case the Thomists are all the less opposed to **Jacob Böhme**; yet nevertheless, a God-enlightened and reborn soul—when, in its **abstraction of the mind from the body** <note>original: *abstractione mentis à corpore* — a state of deep meditation or ecstasy where the mind feels detached from physical sensations.</note>, it looks into the spiritual world of angels—can clearly see these **Powers** <note>original: *Potentias*</note> or "limbs of strength" in its subtle spirit as distinct things. And just as one power is **nobler** than another because of its object, it can also place one "limb" higher than the other. If the angel wishes to speak there, its creaturely essence is its tongue; and the indwelling spirit hears this when, in **abstraction of the mind**, it is "outside the flesh" with **St. Paul** and truly perceives through the ear of its spirit words that are, according to reason, unspeakable. If the angel wishes to see, its **creaturely essence** is its eye, and so the aforementioned spirit of the enlightened person gazes upon it, and so on.

In the meantime, however, he cannot represent such things to the external reason in any other way than through the distinctions of the external limbs in flesh and blood; he must speak of earthly things even while he understands heavenly ones (John 3:12). In this regard, reason stands toward this angelic understanding just as the **imaginative power** <note>original: *vis Phantastica*</note> of an ox stands toward our reason. Therefore, that learned man in his work on **Anthropopathy** <note>original: *Anthropopatheia* — a theological term for attributing human characteristics or emotions to non-human beings, like God or angels.</note> makes this comparison: if a human were to undertake making his human strength understandable to an ox, the ox, in its **imaginative faculty** <note>original: *facultate phantastica*</note>, could not grasp it in any other way than in the animal **form** <note>original: *Specie*</note>, figure, or shape of its horns, in which the ox possesses its strength.

Thus, when that man of God wishes to **represent** to reason the angelic **powers of seeing, hearing, speaking**, etc. <note>original: *potentias visivas, auditivas, locutivas*</note>—which he indeed sees in his enlightened spirit by **intuitive knowledge through their own forms** <note>original: *cognitione intuitiva per species proprias* — direct, immediate spiritual perception of a thing as it is.</note>—he can only [present] these incomprehensible spiritual powers to those fleshly-minded people (who run only by **apprehensive knowledge through foreign forms** <note>original: *cognitione apprehensiva per species alienas* — indirect knowledge gained through metaphors or external images rather than direct experience.</note> in mere reason) through the physical eye, ears, mouth, etc.

The Apostle speaks of the first man’s body in its corruptibility, dishonor, and weakness, and calls this a natural state? Yet he contrasts it with the body of men which shall rise through the power of the resurrected second Adam in incorruptibility, glory, power, and spirituality. But who shall now establish that the first man was *created* in corruptibility, dishonor, and weakness? Rather, that which we had lost in Adam shall be brought back through the Man who is the Lord from heaven. According to the original text, the above words would have read: *The first man Adam became a living soul; the last Adam a life-giving spirit*; but it is not the spiritual that is first, but the soulish <term>soulish<note>The original German uses *seelische*, which corresponds to the Greek *psychikos*. In this context, it refers to the "natural" or "animal" life of the soul as opposed to the higher "spiritual" life (*pneumatikos*).</note>, and thereafter the spiritual. *The first man from the earth (was) earthy-dusty; the second man the Lord from heaven* etc. If Mr. Holtzhausen could believe that the entire Word of God is Spirit and Life, and thus would judge the Holy Scripture spiritually—since it is of a spiritual mind—he might see this more clearly. However, as he gives little hope for this above in the 9th remark and elsewhere (namely, that he can strengthen faith and love in matters where the Scriptures deal with the organs of birth <note>original: *Gebuhrts-Gliedern*</note>), then this divine mystery of the first and second man might shine before his eyes with considerable clarity. This mystery is described in the figure of the birth of Perez and Zerah <note>Perez and Zerah were the twin sons of Tamar and Judah; their unusual birth was often interpreted by mystics as a sign of spiritual priority over physical birthright.</note> in Genesis 38, verses 27 to 30, and is to be explained through the Gospel according to the aforementioned guidance of Dr. Luther. I shall, however, let it rest and leave it to his own judgment; yet the spiritual interpretation of the same, for whoever desires it, can be found in **Jacob Böhme’s** *Mysterium Magnum* <note>Latin: *Great Mystery*</note> or *Explanation of the First Book of Moses*, Chapter 65, paragraphs 58 and 65.

Here once again the blasphemy against the works of **God** is to be noted, namely [Böhme’s claim] that something corrupted was already in Adam before the Fall. Yet Scripture says in Genesis 2 that the **Lord God** caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam even before the Fall, and during that sleep, He built Eve from his ribs before the human Fall into sin occurred. Therefore, all of this belongs to the state of innocence. Böhme, however, wants to reckon it to the state of corruption. As if the sleep had been a death-sleep that would still be continuing now if Eve had not been built; for [he claims] the sleep or the weariness came from the corrupted <term>Salitter</term> in Adam.

## Christian Inquiry into the same.

This has already been dealt with in various places, but specifically <note>original: "in Specie"</note> also in the inquiry of the 9th remark, where the kind reader may look it up.

# XV.

## Jacob Böhme cited from his 12th Chapter, page 146.

Just as Michael was created according to the **quality, nature, and attribute** of **God the Father**, so also was Lucifer created according to the **quality, nature, and beauty** of **God the Son**; and he was bound in love with Him, as a dear son or heart. His heart also stood in the center of the light, just as if he were **God** Himself, and his beauty was above all things. For his embrace, or his most prominent mother, was the **Son of God**; there he stood, as a king or prince of **God**.

## Holzhausen’s Remark.

To say that one angel was created according to the attribute of the **Father** and the other according to the nature of the **Son of God** is not scriptural, but rather a dangerous way of speaking. Böhme’s words strongly imply that Lucifer was also **God** and the **Son of God**, which is a terrible thing to hear.

## Christian Inquiry into the same.

This remark concerning the revelation of the **Triune God** in the angelic world—as well as the idea that Lucifer, in his kingdom of light, creaturely "represented" <note>original: "verweset," which in modern German means to decay, but in this 17th-century context means to act as a representative, administrator, or steward</note> **God** and was created as His creaturely son—has already been Christianly investigated above in the 2nd and 4th remarks of this chapter. It was found to be in harmony with ancient theology <note>original: "heralten Theologia"</note>, as has been shown in various other places. Likewise, the triple hierarchy of the angels as a figure of the **Trinity** is not against Holy Scripture or the **Analogy of Faith** <note>original: "Analogiam fidei," a theological rule that individual bits of scripture must be interpreted in the context of the whole system of faith</note>.

Just as <note>original: "teste Arndio," Latin for "as Arndt testifies," referring to the influential Lutheran theologian Johann Arndt.</note> as Arndt testifies, to see God face to face is the highest joy, the highest life, and the highest bliss; so too is the self-caused (for God is not to blame for it) deprivation of Divine contemplation—fear, anxiety, and terror—the highest sadness, the highest death, and the highest misery and wretchedness. In your own conscience, O vain human! you have a foretaste of this when it awakens, showing how it feels for the devils and damned humans.

## Holtzhausen’s Remark.

Are these not indeed strange speeches to Lucifer? Why should Lucifer kiss the Son of God and then perhaps become whole? For he is indeed a cast-off spirit and has no part in Christ; but belongs among the enemies who shall be made a footstool for the feet of the Son of God. ## Christian Investigation of the Same.

(1) Oh, dear friend! Do let the simple children keep their honest simplicity, who did not expect that such new critics would come who, in their grammar, would turn interjections ("Dear [friend]!") into adjectives <note>The author is poking fun at the critic for over-analyzing Böhme's colloquial or emotional language as if it were formal dogmatic definition.</note>. Furthermore, let (2) the children of God keep their simplicity, and do not take it as a joke when God, through their serene <term>gelaſſen</term> <note>"Gelassenheit" is a central concept in Böhme’s thought, referring to a state of surrendered serenity or "yieldedness" to God's will.</note> spirit, mocks the devil out of righteous judgment. Jacob Böhme—or rather, the Spirit of God through him—rightly mocks the wretched devil; but you wrongly mock the children of God, or rather the Spirit of God within them, and turn their precious divine mysteries into Pickelhäring’s antics <note>Pickelhäring was a popular stock comedic character in 17th-century German theater; the author is accusing the critic of treating sacred matters like a low-brow comedy.</note>, devilish mockeries, and delusions of the head and brain.

## Holtzhausen’s Note.

Here we see how he presents Lucifer as a king who arose from the eternal Source-Spirits, which are supposed to be a piece of the Godhead. Should one thus divide the eternal Godhead into pieces, and attribute to one piece thereof that it rebelled and sinned against the whole God? It is indeed terrible talk to say that the seven Source-Spirits are to have no beginning, are to be a piece of the Godhead, and yet could rise up against God and thus become a devil.

## Christian Investigation of the Same.

Holtzhausen here confuses the seven Source-Spirits according to their eternal uncreatureliness <note>the state of being part of the divine essence before being shaped into a specific being</note> and according to their creatureliness <note>the state of being a distinct, created entity</note>. In the former, there is an essential unity in the center of the Godhead; but here, in the state of a creature, a real division and separation can indeed take place. This was clearly enough distinguished and untangled above, at the beginning of this second chapter and in several investigations of the notes that followed.
